title: Meet
subtitle: 「見面／遇見／碰面」，究竟是哪一種 meet？
description: 「見面／遇見／碰面」，究竟是哪一種 meet？

words.note: 較正式，表示遇到某人，既可指偶然碰面，也可指較一般的相遇；比日常 meet 稍正式。
words.example: She encountered an old colleague at the conference.
words.exampleZh: 她在會議上遇到一位舊同事。

exercises.original: She met an old colleague unexpectedly at the conference.
exercises.zh: 她在會議上意外遇到一位舊同事。
exercises.upgrade: encounter · 遇見；碰到

options.explanation: visited = visit 表示專程拜訪；本句是 unexpectedly 偶然遇到。
contacted = contact 可以是電話或訊息，不表示當面碰見。
encounter = unexpectedly 是關鍵線索；較正式地描述一次偶然相遇，可用 encountered。
knew = know 表示已認識，不能表達這次相遇。
joined = join 是加入某人或群體，不是遇見。
greeted = greet 是相遇後打招呼，不是相遇本身。

exercises.original: During the field trip, the researchers met several local farmers.
exercises.zh: 實地考察期間，研究人員遇到了幾位當地農民。
exercises.upgrade: encounter · 遇見；碰到

options.explanation: visited = 本句沒有說研究人員到農民家中拜訪。
contacted = 不表示實際在 field trip 中相遇。
joined = 沒有加入農民群體的意思。
encounter = field trip 中實際遇見當地人，正式敘述可自然用 encountered。
greeted = 只表示問候。
knew = 不表示這一次碰面。

exercises.original: He met a former client by chance while travelling overseas.
exercises.zh: 他在海外旅行時偶然遇到一位以前的客戶。
exercises.upgrade: encounter · 遇見；碰到

options.explanation: visited = by chance 排除專程拜訪。
contacted = 聯絡不等於旅行途中碰見。
saw = 可用，但 encountered 更能配合 by chance 的偶然相遇語感。
joined = 不合。
encounter = by chance 明確表示偶然相遇，因此 encountered 很精確。
greeted = 只描述相遇之後的問候。

words.note: 表示有意安排和某人見面、相聚或一起活動，語氣自然、口語，通常不是偶然碰見。
words.example: We get together with our neighbours once a month.
words.exampleZh: 我們每月和鄰居聚會一次。

exercises.original: We meet our neighbours once a month for dinner.
exercises.zh: 我們每月和鄰居聚餐一次。
exercises.upgrade: get together with · 與……聚會；相聚

options.explanation: encounter = encounter 常帶偶然意味；每月聚餐是固定安排。
come across = 表示偶然碰見，不符合 once a month 的安排。
contact = 聯絡不代表一起吃飯。
get together with = once a month for dinner 是有意安排的社交聚會，因此 get together with 最自然。
greet = 打招呼不足以表示整晚聚餐。
visit = 可能包含見面，但本句重點是雙方相聚。

exercises.original: The old friends meet every summer for a weekend by the lake.
exercises.zh: 這群老朋友每年夏天都在湖邊相聚一個週末。
exercises.upgrade: get together with · 與……聚會；相聚

options.explanation: run into = run into 是偶然碰見，不會每年固定安排。
see = 可泛指見面，但不能同樣突出大家聚在一起一段時間。
contact = 不表示實際共度週末。
greet = 只是問候。
get together with = 一群朋友固定相聚並共度時間，get together 最貼切。
cross paths = 帶偶然性，不符合固定 annual plan。

exercises.original: Our team meets socially after major projects are completed.
exercises.zh: 我們團隊在大型項目完成後會相聚聯誼。
exercises.upgrade: get together with · 與……聚會；相聚

options.explanation: encounters = 不是偶然遇到團隊成員。
contacts = 不表示大家實際聚在一起。
visits = 沒有誰拜訪誰的明確方向。
greets = 只是打招呼。
knows = 不是相聚事件。
get together with = socially 表示非正式相聚，因此 gets together 比一般 meets 更具體。

words.note: 日常英語中非常常見，可表示安排好去見某人，尤其是朋友、醫生、客戶或同事；是否屬正式會面取決於語境。
words.example: I'm seeing my dentist tomorrow morning.

exercises.original: I'm meeting my dentist tomorrow morning.
exercises.zh: 我明早會去見牙醫。
exercises.upgrade: see · 見；與……見面

options.explanation: encountering = 預約牙醫不是偶然相遇。
coming across = 帶偶然性，不合 appointment。
greeting = 不是只去打招呼。
joining = 不是加入牙醫。
see = 日常英語中，安排好去見 doctor/dentist 很常用 see。
knowing = 不表示明天的會面。

exercises.original: She's meeting a client after lunch to discuss the proposal.
exercises.zh: 她午飯後會見客戶，討論建議書。
exercises.upgrade: see · 見；與……見面

options.explanation: running into = run into 是偶遇，和 to discuss the proposal 的安排不符。
contacting = 可能不面對面。
greeting = 不夠表示正式交談。
joining = 不合。
knowing = 不表示這次 appointment。
see = 在已安排的客戶會面語境中，see a client 是自然用法。

exercises.original: I haven't met my cousins for months, so I'm going to meet them this weekend.
exercises.zh: 我幾個月沒有見表親了，所以這個週末會去見他們。
exercises.upgrade: see · 見；與……見面

options.explanation: see = 已認識的親友之間談『很久沒見』和安排再見面，最自然用 see。
encountered = 不是偶然相遇。
contacted = 不一定面對面。
greeted = 太短暫。
joined = 不表示探望／見面。
met for the first time = 表親早已認識，不是初次相識。

words.note: 表示沒有事先安排而偶然遇見某人；也可表示偶然發現物品或資訊。
words.example: I came across an old classmate at the airport.
words.exampleZh: 我在機場偶然遇到一位舊同學。

exercises.original: I met an old classmate by chance at the airport.
exercises.zh: 我在機場偶然遇到一位舊同學。
exercises.upgrade: come across · 偶然遇到；碰見

options.explanation: met up with = meet up with 通常是預先約好，不符合 by chance。
had a meeting with = 太正式且表示安排好的會議。
visited = 不是專程拜訪。
contacted = 不表示當面遇見。
joined = 不合。
come across = by chance 明確表示偶然遇到，因此 came across 很自然。

exercises.original: She met a former neighbour while shopping downtown.
exercises.zh: 她在市中心購物時偶然遇到以前的鄰居。
exercises.upgrade: come across · 偶然遇到；碰見

options.explanation: come across = shopping 時沒有預先安排的相遇，可自然說 came across。
saw = 可表示見到，但 came across 更突出偶然相遇。
met with = 通常表示安排好的會面。
visited = 不是到對方家拜訪。
greeted = 只表示打招呼。
joined = 不合。

exercises.original: We met a group of hikers unexpectedly on the trail.
exercises.zh: 我們在步道上意外遇到一群遠足者。
exercises.upgrade: come across · 偶然遇到；碰見

options.explanation: met up with = 暗示約好碰面。
come across = 在 trail 上偶然碰見其他人，came across 很貼切。
had a meeting with = 完全不合遠足偶遇語境。
contacted = 不表示在 trail 實際碰到。
visited = 不合。
knew = 不表示此次偶遇。

words.note: 很常見的口語說法，表示意外遇見熟人，通常沒有預先安排。
words.example: She ran into her former teacher at the supermarket.
words.exampleZh: 她在超級市場偶然碰見以前的老師。

exercises.original: I met my former teacher unexpectedly at the supermarket.
exercises.zh: 我在超級市場意外碰見以前的老師。
exercises.upgrade: run into · 偶然碰見

options.explanation: run into = supermarket + unexpectedly 是典型口語偶遇場景，因此 ran into 最自然。
met with = 通常是有安排、有目的的會面。
visited = 不是專程拜訪老師。
contacted = 不是電話或訊息聯絡。
joined = 不合。
introduced myself to = former teacher 已經認識，不是初次介紹。

exercises.original: She met an old friend on the train home.
exercises.zh: 她回家乘火車時偶然碰見一位舊朋友。
exercises.upgrade: run into · 偶然碰見

options.explanation: met up with = 若沒有約好，不應用這個片語。
run into = 日常交通途中偶遇熟人，口語通常說 run into。
had a meeting with = 太正式。
contacted = 不表示實際相遇。
visited = 不合。
greeted = 只是見面後的一個動作。

exercises.original: We met our old landlord by accident outside the cinema.
exercises.zh: 我們在戲院外意外碰到以前的房東。
exercises.upgrade: run into · 偶然碰見

options.explanation: saw = 可表示看見，但不如 ran into 強調意外碰面。
met with = 暗示安排。
run into = by accident 直接支持 ran into 這種非正式偶遇說法。
visited = 不是拜訪。
contacted = 不是遠距聯絡。
joined = 不合。

words.note: 較口語，表示和某人預先約好碰面，常見於朋友、同事或非正式活動。
words.example: I'm meeting up with some friends after work.
words.exampleZh: 我下班後會和幾個朋友碰面。

exercises.original: I'm meeting some friends after work for coffee.
exercises.zh: 我下班後會和幾個朋友碰面喝咖啡。
exercises.upgrade: meet up with · 與……碰面；相約見面

options.explanation: running into = run into 是偶然碰見，而本句有 after work for coffee 的安排。
meet up with = 朋友預先約好 after work 喝咖啡，meet up with 最自然。
encountering = 較正式且常帶偶然意味。
contacting = 不一定實際見面。
greeting = 只表示問候。
visiting = 不一定是去某人的住處，也沒有聚會語感。

exercises.original: We met our study group at the library before the exam.
exercises.zh: 考試前我們和學習小組在圖書館碰面。
exercises.upgrade: meet up with · 與……碰面；相約見面

options.explanation: came across = 表示偶遇，不符合 study group 的安排。
crossed paths with = 也帶偶然性。
meet up with = study group 在指定地點相約碰面，口語用 met up with 很貼切。
contacted = 不是遠距聯絡。
greeted = 沒有一起學習的意思。
joined = 可表示加入小組，但不等同約定見面。

exercises.original: She met her cousin in town before they went to the concert.
exercises.zh: 她在市中心和表親碰面，之後一起去音樂會。
exercises.upgrade: meet up with · 與……碰面；相約見面

options.explanation: ran into = 會表示意外碰見，不符合之後一起去 concert 的安排。
encountered = 太正式且偏偶遇。
contacted = 不表示當面。
meet up with = 兩人先約好碰面再一起去活動，met up with 很自然。
greeted = 只表示打招呼。
visited = 不合 town meeting point。

words.note: 常用於較正式或有目的的會面，例如和客戶、主管、官員或顧問討論事情。
words.example: The manager met with the project team to discuss the delay.
words.exampleZh: 經理與項目團隊會面，討論延誤問題。

exercises.original: The manager met the project team to discuss the delay.
exercises.zh: 經理與項目團隊會面，討論延誤問題。
exercises.upgrade: meet with · 與……會面；商談

options.explanation: ran into = 不是偶然碰見。
came across = 同樣帶偶然性。
meet with = to discuss the delay 表示有明確工作目的，因此 met with 很自然。
greeted = 不足以表達正式討論。
visited = 未必是拜訪。
knew = 不表示這次會面。

exercises.original: The minister will meet community representatives tomorrow.
exercises.zh: 部長明天會與社區代表會面。
exercises.upgrade: meet with · 與……會面；商談

options.explanation: see = 口語可用，但正式官員會面更自然用 meet with。
run into = 帶偶然意味。
come across = 不合預定 official meeting。
meet with = 官員與 representatives 的預定會談屬正式語境，meet with 最精確。
greet = 不等於正式會談。
join = 不合。

exercises.original: She met her adviser to review the research plan.
exercises.zh: 她與導師會面，檢視研究計劃。
exercises.upgrade: meet with · 與……會面；商談

options.explanation: came across = 不是偶遇。
ran into = 不合有目的的 review。
greeted = 只表示問候。
contacted = 可能不是面對面。
meet with = to review the research plan 是明確會面目的，因此 met with 很合適。
visited = 未必涉及到訪。

words.note: 比 meet with 更明確地表示一次安排好的正式會議，通常有特定議題或工作目的。
words.example: She had a meeting with the supplier about the new contract.
words.exampleZh: 她與供應商就新合約開會。

exercises.original: I met the supplier this morning to discuss the new contract.
exercises.zh: 我今早與供應商開會討論新合約。
exercises.upgrade: have a meeting with · 與……開會；會面

options.explanation: ran into = 不是偶然碰見。
came across = 不合 contract discussion。
greeted = 太短暫，沒有正式討論。
have a meeting with = to discuss the new contract 顯示這是一場有明確議題的正式會議，因此 had a meeting with 最精確。
visited = 可能去對方辦公室，但不等於開會。
contacted = 也可能透過電話或電郵。

exercises.original: The department head met the auditors before the final report was issued.
exercises.zh: 部門主管在最終報告發出前與核數師開會。
exercises.upgrade: have a meeting with · 與……開會；會面

options.explanation: met up with = 太口語，像朋友相約。
ran into = 不合專業審計安排。
greeted = 不表示正式討論。
joined = 不合。
have a meeting with = department head + auditors 是正式工作會議，因此 had a meeting with 很自然。
knew = 不表示這次事件。

exercises.original: She met her supervisor for an hour about the budget.
exercises.zh: 她與主管就預算開了一小時會議。
exercises.upgrade: have a meeting with · 與……開會；會面

options.explanation: saw = 可泛指見面，但 for an hour about the budget 更明確是一場 meeting。
came across = 不是偶遇。
contacted = 不一定當面。
greeted = 太短暫。
visited = 不表示討論 budget。
have a meeting with = for an hour about the budget 明確描述一場安排好的會議，因此這個說法最精確。

words.note: 當 meet 指第一次在他人介紹下認識某人時最精確；不是一般再次見面。
words.example: I was introduced to the new director at lunch.
words.exampleZh: 我在午餐時被介紹認識新任主管。

exercises.original: I met the new director for the first time at lunch.
exercises.zh: 我在午餐時第一次被介紹認識新任主管。
exercises.upgrade: be introduced to · 被介紹認識；初次見到

options.explanation: saw = see 只表示見到，不能確保是第一次正式認識。
met with = 偏向有目的會談，而非首次介紹。
ran into = 表示偶遇。
contacted = 不表示正式被介紹。
be introduced to = for the first time + social introduction 的語境最自然用 was introduced to。
visited = 不合。

exercises.original: She met her partner's parents at a family dinner.
exercises.zh: 她在家庭晚餐中被介紹認識伴侶的父母。
exercises.upgrade: be introduced to · 被介紹認識；初次見到

options.explanation: came across = 不是偶然碰見陌生人。
met up with = 較像早已認識後相約。
contacted = 不表示面對面介紹。
greeted = 只是介紹後可能發生的問候。
joined = 不合。
be introduced to = 家庭晚餐中第一次正式認識 partner's parents，was introduced to 很精確。

exercises.original: At the reception, he met several senior executives he had never spoken to before.
exercises.zh: 在招待會上，他被介紹認識幾位以前從未交談過的高級行政人員。
exercises.upgrade: be introduced to · 被介紹認識；初次見到

options.explanation: be introduced to = reception + had never spoken to before 指首次正式相識，因此 was introduced to 最自然。
saw = 只是看見，不表示建立認識。
ran into = 太偶然、太口語。
met with = 像安排好的正式討論。
contacted = 不表示面對面。
visited = 不合 reception。

words.meaning: 認識某人；與某人初次相識
words.note: 較正式、略帶書面語，表示第一次認識某人；常用於較正式或禮貌語境。
words.example: I first made her acquaintance at a charity dinner.
words.exampleZh: 我第一次認識她是在一場慈善晚宴上。

exercises.original: I first met her at a charity dinner many years ago.
exercises.zh: 多年前，我第一次在慈善晚宴上認識她。
exercises.upgrade: make someone's acquaintance · 認識某人；與某人初次相識

options.explanation: visited her = 表示拜訪她，不是首次相識。
contacted her = 不一定當面，也沒有正式初識語感。
greeted her = 只表示問候。
joined her = 表示加入她，不合。
saw her = 只是看見，不一定建立認識。
make someone's acquaintance = first + charity dinner 是較正式的初次相識語境，made her acquaintance 很自然。

exercises.original: He met the professor through a mutual friend.
exercises.zh: 他透過共同朋友認識了那位教授。
exercises.upgrade: make someone's acquaintance · 認識某人；與某人初次相識

options.explanation: make someone's acquaintance = through a mutual friend 表示被引介後初次認識，正式可用 make someone's acquaintance。
visited the professor = 不是去拜訪。
contacted the professor = 不等於實際相識。
greeted the professor = 只是打招呼。
ran into the professor = 會表示偶然遇見，和 through a mutual friend 不同。
joined the professor = 不合。

exercises.original: She first met several local artists while attending the opening reception.
exercises.zh: 她在參加開幕酒會時首次認識幾位本地藝術家。
exercises.upgrade: make someone's acquaintance · 認識某人；與某人初次相識

options.explanation: visited several local artists = 不是拜訪。
make someone's acquaintance = opening reception 是偏正式社交場合，描述首次相識可用 made the acquaintance of。
contacted several local artists = 未必當面。
saw several local artists = 只表示看見。
greeted several local artists = 只描述問候。
joined several local artists = 不合。

words.note: 表示兩人的行程意外交會而碰面，常帶『碰巧』意味；比 run into 稍形象化。
words.example: I crossed paths with an old neighbour while travelling abroad.
words.exampleZh: 我在海外旅行時碰巧遇到一位舊鄰居。

exercises.original: I met an old neighbour unexpectedly while travelling abroad.
exercises.zh: 我在海外旅行時意外碰到一位舊鄰居。
exercises.upgrade: cross paths with · 與……不期而遇；碰巧遇上

options.explanation: cross paths with = 兩人的行程在海外意外交會，crossed paths with 很形象自然。
met up with = 通常表示預先約好。
had a meeting with = 太正式且有議題目的。
visited = 不是專程拜訪。
contacted = 不表示實際相遇。
joined = 不合。

exercises.original: She met her former manager again by chance at a railway station.
exercises.zh: 她在火車站再次偶然遇到以前的經理。
exercises.upgrade: cross paths with · 與……不期而遇；碰巧遇上

options.explanation: saw = 可以表示見到，但不突出雙方行程偶然交會。
cross paths with = by chance + railway station 很適合 crossed paths with。
met with = 帶預定會談意味。
visited = 不合 railway station。
greeted = 只是相遇後問候。
contacted = 不是當面相遇。

exercises.original: The two researchers met unexpectedly at another conference years later.
exercises.zh: 多年後，兩名研究人員又在另一場會議上意外碰面。
exercises.upgrade: cross paths with · 與……不期而遇；碰巧遇上

options.explanation: met up = 暗示預先約定。
had a meeting = 不表示 unexpected reunion。
cross paths with = 多年後在另一場合偶然再遇，crossed paths again 很自然。
contacted each other = 不一定面對面。
visited each other = 不合 conference。
joined each other = 不自然。

words.note: 較正式或帶特定語感，表示在預定時間和地點與某人會合；常見於旅行、軍事、行動計劃或較書面的敘述。
words.example: The rescue team rendezvoused with the guides near the river.
words.exampleZh: 救援隊在河邊與嚮導會合。

exercises.original: The rescue team met the local guides near the river at the agreed time.
exercises.zh: 救援隊在約定時間於河邊與當地嚮導會合。
exercises.upgrade: rendezvous with · 與……在約定地點會合

options.explanation: ran into = run into 是偶然碰見，和 agreed time 相反。
rendezvous with = near the river at the agreed time 明確表示在約定時間地點會合，因此 rendezvoused with 最精確。
came across = 同樣偏偶遇。
visited = 不是到嚮導住所拜訪。
greeted = 只表示問候。
contacted = 不表示實際在指定地點會合。

exercises.original: The two patrols met at the checkpoint before continuing together.
exercises.zh: 兩支巡邏隊在檢查站會合，之後一起繼續前進。
exercises.upgrade: rendezvous with · 與……在約定地點會合

options.explanation: encountered = 可表示相遇，但不一定是預先安排。
ran into = 過於口語且帶偶然性。
rendezvous with = 兩支隊伍在 checkpoint 集合後共同前進，正式行動語境可用 rendezvoused。
contacted = 不等於實際會合。
greeted = 不是核心動作。
visited = 不合 checkpoint。

exercises.original: The hikers met their driver at the agreed pickup point after sunset.
exercises.zh: 遠足者在日落後於約定接送點與司機會合。
exercises.upgrade: rendezvous with · 與……在約定地點會合

options.explanation: came across = 若是 agreed pickup point，就不是偶然。
ran into = 同樣帶偶然意味。
visited = 不是拜訪司機。
rendezvous with = agreed pickup point 是預定時間／地點會合的強烈線索，因此 rendezvoused with 很自然。
greeted = 只是碰面後的問候。
knew = 不表示此次會合。

falseSynonyms.zh: 拜訪不一定等於見面 visit 強調前往某人或某地並停留一段時間；meet 只要求雙方碰面。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON You can meet someone briefly without visiting them.

falseSynonyms.zh: 聯絡不等於見面 contact 可以透過電話、電郵或訊息完成，不一定面對面。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON You can contact a client without meeting them in person.

falseSynonyms.zh: 認識不等於見面 know 表示已經認識或了解某人；meet 可指第一次相識或一次具體會面。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON You may know someone for years but meet them only occasionally.

falseSynonyms.zh: 加入不等於遇見 join 表示加入某人、群體或活動；並不自動表示初次或偶然碰面。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON She joined the group after meeting them in the lobby.

falseSynonyms.zh: 打招呼不等於見面 greet 是見到某人後向對方問候；meet 是相遇或會面的事件本身。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON They met at the entrance and greeted each other warmly.

falseSynonyms.zh: 動詞與名詞不同 meet 是動詞；meeting 通常是名詞，表示會議或會面，也可作動名詞。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON We meet every Friday. The meeting starts at ten.

falseSynonyms.zh: 正式程度與偶然性不同 encounter 較正式，而且常帶偶然或非預期相遇的意味；meet 的範圍更廣。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON We arranged to meet at noon, but I encountered him unexpectedly the day before.

falseSynonyms.zh: 見面與初次認識不完全相同 see 很常用於已認識的人之間安排見面；若強調第一次認識某人，通常仍用 meet 或 be introduced to。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON I'm seeing Anna tomorrow, but I first met her last year.
